question_text: Forests are the best case studies for economic excellence.
customKeyPointers: A forest compounds value instead of spending the capital
Excellence here is a yield that does not end the source
An economy that clear-cuts its stock is not excellent

points.text: A forest is an economy that has already solved the problem of lasting.
It produces timber, water, a soil and a climate together, and it does so by recycling its own waste.
No single species maximises this year's output at the cost of the next decade. That restraint is the excellence.
A human economy that copies only the harvest, and not the regeneration, has studied the forest badly.
The case study is useful for a farm, a firm and a national account: measure what remains, not only what was cut.
Economic excellence is a forest's kind of profit: a return that leaves the capital standing.

question_text: Poets are the unacknowledged legislators of the world.
customKeyPointers: A law states a rule; a poem makes a feeling look obvious
People obey the feeling long before they obey the statute
Unacknowledged does not mean unimportant

points.text: Shelley's line means that poets fix the moral imagination which later laws only write down.
A phrase for dignity, grief or a nation enters ordinary speech and then enters a constitution.
The poet does not sit in a house of assembly. The assembly later speaks in the poet's metaphors.
This power can also narrow a people, if the only songs they know are of hate or of a single glory.
Acknowledgement is rare because the legislation happens in the language, years before the vote.
Poets legislate the possible. Parliaments legislate the permitted.

question_text: History is a series of victories won by the scientific man over the romantic man.
customKeyPointers: The line claims that method keeps beating feeling
Many advances were a measurement winning over a myth
The romantic mind also won some of the freedoms the scientific mind lives inside

points.text: The claim is half true: science has repeatedly corrected a beautiful error.
Medicine, a crop and a bridge replaced a charm, and the correction saved lives.
The romantic man is not only the enemy of the fact. The demand for equality, a nation, and a dignity science did not invent came from that side.
A victory of the scientific man that has no romance becomes a technique without a purpose.
The useful reading is a partnership in which the measurement leads and the human end is not discarded.
History is not a clean series of those victories. It is the argument between them.

question_text: A ship in harbour is safe, but that is not what ship is for.
customKeyPointers: Safety is a condition, not a vocation
A ship exists to cross, and a crossing has weather
Recklessness is not the alternative; an unused safety is the failure

points.text: The sentence separates being unharmed from having done the thing one exists to do.
A harbour is necessary. A ship that never leaves has mistaken the harbour for the voyage.
The same is true of a student, a firm and a country: a capacity that is never used in the world it was built for is only a stored fear.
The wisdom is to leave with a hull, a chart and a crew, not to leave in order to be brave.
Staying can be right in a storm. Staying as a permanent policy is a different, smaller life.
Ships are for the crossing. Safety is how they become fit to attempt it.

question_text: The time to repair the roof is when the sun is shining.
customKeyPointers: A leak is cheapest to fix before the rain
Good years are when a surplus is spent on the weakness
A crisis is a bad workshop

points.text: Kennedy's sentence is a rule of public and private prudence.
A bank, a hospital, a granary and a skill are repaired in the year they are not being desperately used.
A boom that is entirely consumed leaves the roof for the recession, when money and attention are gone.
The same applies to a relationship, a health and a constitution: the convenient time is the time.
Waiting for the rain to prove the need is how preventable damage becomes a disaster.
The shining day is not the holiday from maintenance. It is the appointment for it.

question_text: You cannot step twice in the same river.
customKeyPointers: The water has moved, and so has the person stepping in
Identity survives change; it is not a frozen thing
The line does not say that nothing continues

points.text: The sentence says that recurrence is an illusion of the name.
The river keeps the name and replaces the water. A person keeps the name and replaces the cells, the opinions and the debts.
Treating a nation, a party or oneself as the same substance forever is how reform is refused.
What continues is the channel: a constitution, a character, a direction. What cannot be repeated is the moment.
Wisdom is to step in knowingly, as a changed person into a changed stream.
You return to the river. You do not return to the same water.

question_text: A smile is the chosen vehicle for all ambiguities.
customKeyPointers: A smile can mean warmth, fear, irony or a refusal
It is chosen because it is socially safe and hard to pin down
The line is about language as much as about the face

points.text: A smile carries meanings that a plain sentence would be punished for.
In a court, a home and a negotiation, the smile lets a person disagree without a declared war.
That is its kindness and its danger: a cruelty, a contempt and a plea can wear the same mouth.
Ambiguity is sometimes the only honest report of a mixed feeling, and the smile is how it travels.
A public life that reads every smile as consent will miss the ambiguity the smile was sent to hold.
The vehicle is chosen because everyone sees it and no one is forced to fix its meaning.

question_text: Just because you have a choice, it does not mean that any of them has to be right.
customKeyPointers: A menu is not a moral fact
Having options can hide the absence of a good one
Sometimes the right act is to refuse the list

points.text: The sentence warns against treating the existence of options as evidence that one of them is worthy.
A bad law, a rigged market and a cruel order can all be offered as a choice.
The chooser is then blamed for the outcome, as if the list had contained a right answer.
Ethics begins by asking who wrote the options, and whether none is allowed.
In private life the same trap appears as a forced career, a forced silence or a forced loyalty.
A choice proves only that more than one path was shown. It does not prove that any path was right.
